articles.title: How ‘Ink’ Production Designers Recreated The Sun Newsroom Using Functional Linotype Machines, Working Rotary Phones and Old Typewriters
articles.summary: Danny Boyle’s latest film “Ink” traces the rise of Rupert Murdoch on London’s Fleet Street and the takeover of The Sun newspaper. The film premieres at the London Film Festival and will open in select theaters Dec. 11 before landing on Netflix on Jan. 8 in the U.S. and Latin America.
body: Danny Boyle ’s latest film “ Ink ” traces the rise of Rupert Murdoch on London’s Fleet Street and the takeover of The Sun newspaper.
The Fleet Street of today looks vastly different from the Fleet Street of 1969. “A lot of Fleet Street doesn’t exist anymore,” Pugh says.

The Sun’s 1969 headquarters was originally located on Bouverie Street, with the print press set in the basement of the offices. In its place now stand modern buildings. “We ran into challenges when trying to recreate the newsroom,” Pugh says.

They ultimately found a space in Bromley, U.K., which they could transform for filming. “It had been vacated by the local council, and the mix of different architectural styles made it ideal for housing the various set-pieces, particularly the newsroom,” he explains.

articles.title: Alex Gibney says Universal ‘wavered’ over releasing Elon Musk documentary
articles.summary: The revelation comes after the four-hour film’s Venice premiere drew a string of criticisms and insults from the founder of SpaceXAI. Alex Gibney, director of the new four-hour documentary about Elon Musk, said that Universal, owners of the film’s international distribution rights “wavered” over…
body: Gibney was speaking to the New York Times as the film opened in the US (where it is being released by the independent distributor Bleecker Street), and appeared to confirm a story in the Hollywood Reporter that Universal, which had acquired the international rights to the film in 2023, had got cold feet. Asked by the New York Times, “Did Universal Pictures waver in setting up its international release plans?” Gibney replied: “Yes.”

A subsequent story in Variety suggested that Universal had been concerned about “legal threats from Musk”, but that the studio had “always been enthusiastic about releasing the film internationally”. Gibney was asked: “So it wasn’t about legal clearances?” The film-maker replied: “You can walk and chew gum at the same time.”
However, it appears plans are back on track, as Gibney added: “We just had a meeting with [Universal], and we’re talking very concretely about a release plan.”

articles.title: Katherine Mallen Kupferer, Audrey Grace Marshall, Dean Norris, Jordan Ladd Join ‘The Attentionist’ from Caroline Kepnes (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Caroline Kepnes, author of the novel series “You,” which inspired the global Netflix hit, has assembled a team of buzzy actors for her series directorial debut. Katherine Mallen Kupferer, Audrey Grace Marshall, Dean Norris and Jordan Ladd will star in “The Attentionist,” a digital-first project…
body: “The Attentionist” is set in a ‘90s Cape Cod neighborhood where the coastal elite live side by side with seasonal summer residents. The story picks up when 14-year-old Maeve and her older sister, Reg, start a secret phone romance with a boy from the local boat club who promises a way into the upper echelons of Cape Cod society. But when the voice on the phone takes a dark turn, Maeve keeps listening, pulling her family further into a monstrous secret.

Kepnes serves as writer and director for “The Attentionist.” Mark Roberts of Roberts Media (“Meet Me Next Christmas”) and Lorena David (“Strangers with Candy”) serve as producers. The project, which will shoot on location in Kepnes’ native Cape Cod, is set for release on YouTube.

”The heart of this story is a total genre clash. One minute it’s this awkward ’90s oceanside family comedy, and the next it plunges into raw psychological dread,” Kepnes said. “To pull that off, I needed a family that felt completely real and delightfully chaotic. Watching Dean, Jordan, Katherine and Audrey bring these dynamics to life as unseen terror creeps into their lives is everything I hoped it would be.”

articles.title: ABC Alleges FCC’s Attempts to Curb Its Free Speech Were Designed to Evade Judicial Review
articles.summary: ABC, in a new filing in its First Amendment lawsuit against the FCC, claims that the agency’s early-license renewal demand for its local TV stations was done in such a way as to circumvent “judicial review.” On Aug.
body: On Monday, ABC responded to the FCC’s filing. The FCC had argued at the hearing that “‘the license renewal process is not about the licenses,’ but rather an attempt to deal with what they claim to be a discovery deficiency” in the DEI probe, the network says in the fling. “But their supplemental briefing only confirms what they conceded at the hearing: there are ‘a number of different tools’ by which the agency could have addressed the purported discovery deficiency.”

ABC continued: “These are not merely ‘theoretical[]’ tools… they have been used by the agency for decades. Yet the agency tried none of those less intrusive tools here, instead taking the unprecedented step of calling for early license renewal of all eight ABC-owned stations at once. Defendants’ own admissions leave no doubt as to why — Defendants sought to inflict maximal coercive pressure on the media company whose speech the Administration sought to curb, while deliberately evading judicial review.”

articles.title: Ben Affleck Calls ‘Justice League’ Reshoots the ‘Low Point of My Career’: ‘It Was So Gross’ How the Studio Replaced Zack Snyder With Joss Whedon
articles.summary: Ben Affleck appeared on the latest episode of the “Happy Sad Confused” podcast and called the reshoots for “Justice League” the “low point of my career.” Warner Bros. infamously replaced director Zack Snyder with Joss Whedon to overhaul the movie after Snyder needed to pause work due to his…
body: “Somebody’s death by suicide eclipses everything,” Affleck continued, referring to the death of Snyder’s daughter. “The way in which that was, I thought, used as an excuse [to replace Zack] was one of the shittiest things I’ve ever seen. It was so gross. The whole environment and vibe [on set during the reshoots], much of which I was not privy to but heard secondhand from the actors, it was just, ‘Wow, this is about as gross as it gets.’ And I was drinking too much… and I got divorced. It was a difficult time for me personally, but those thing, while painful, did not impact that movie.”

Affleck previously told Entertainment Weekly that making “Justice League” was “a nadir experience” that made him not want to continue playing Batman. The actor added at the time: “I didn’t like being there. I didn’t think it was interesting. And then some really shitty things, awful things happened. But, that’s when I was like, I’m not going to do that anymore.”

articles.title: Digger on course for $245m loss after box office collapse
articles.summary: Estimates suggest the eco satire starring Tom Cruise could join the list of top turkeys, including Cutthroat Island and The Marvels. Digger, the ambitious eco-fable starring Tom Cruise and directed by Alejandro G Iñárritu, is heading for an even worse financial outcome than previously thought, with…
body: According to a report in Variety, Digger’s estimated second weekend revenue in North America of $3.2m is a 60% drop on its opening weekend figure of $8m, meaning its current domestic gross is $14.4m, for a global total of $35.3m, with a projected final box office total of around $50m worldwide.
A $245m loss would put Digger on a par with such legendary turkeys as Cutthroat Island ($222m loss, adjusted for inflation), Mortal Engines ($224m adjusted) and The Marvels ($205-$250m adjusted).

Reaction to the film has likely played a key role in its underperformance, with critical opinion radically divided. In the Guardian, chief film critic Peter Bradshaw called it “an exasperatingly shallow, laborious, self-congratulatory satire” in a two-star review, while Guardian Australia’s deputy culture editor Sian Cain took the opposite position, describing it as “a masterpiece”. Warner Bros, whose last release this is before its takeover by David Ellison’s Skydance, tried to play into the controversy with a post-release advertising campaign quoting its negative notices, but it seems to have had little effect.

articles.title: Hallowarrior review – apocalyptic Home Alone-style survival horror delivers inventive shocks
articles.summary: Debut feature from Ben Sottak provides outlandish Halloween-based scares, with Milly Shapiro superb as the naive yet resilient home-defender, Pumpkin. Home Alone meets Mad Max in this atmospheric seasonal chiller, named for Halloween and not a cheery greeting.
body: It’s the first major screen role for Shapiro since her memorable debut as the little sister in Ari Aster’s Hereditary, and she is in almost every scene here, making for quite the showcase. It’s good casting: Pumpkin is an intriguing presence – at once young and old, presumably because she’s been fending for herself during such a key stage of her development. She’s not had any adult guidance since the age of 12 – arresting her development in some ways, while having to survive, be totally independent and grieve her entire family alone has simultaneously made her unusually tough in others.

articles.title: ‘A rare indulgence’: why Black Swan is my feelgood movie
articles.summary: The latest in our series of writers explaining their go-to comfort films is a tribute to Darren Aronofsky’s dark and unusually satisfying ballet nightmare. In early 2011, sometime after the film was released on home video, I sat down with mum to watch what she had heard was a “new ballet movie” by…
body: Well before Brendan Fraser’s time on the couch and the many houseguests of Mother!, Aronofsky increased the wattage with a companion piece to follow his heavy-hitter, The Wrestler. Watching Nina Sayers’ (Portman) intense physical trials and her stilted sexual awakening, with my mum beside me, I was understandably disturbed. At this point in my adolescence, I thought Jumanji was a scary movie. Like the film’s injured bird, I was being introduced to a darkness I didn’t understand. And somehow I couldn’t get enough. Why did it feel so good?

In the years since, I have returned to Black Swan in search of that same dread and delight. With each viewing, my affection for it deepens. The pale pinks and gentle powdery blues, Nina’s cosy wrap sweaters and leotards, even Barbara Hershey’s smothering presence, all of it has become an unexpected comfort.

articles.title: Tom Cruise film Digger forecast to become one of Hollywood's biggest flops
articles.summary: The film dropped by around 60% in its second weekend, and could become one of Hollywood's biggest flops.
body: Tom Cruise's latest film Digger is expected to lose around $245m (£185m), Hollywood analysts have said, after the film's continuing poor performance at the box office.
Ticket sales for the satirical black comedy, which stars Cruise as oil magnate Digger Rockwell, dropped by around 60% in the movie's second weekend in cinemas.
It brings Digger's total box office takings so far to around $35m (£26m) globally. The film is estimated to have cost its studio Warner Bros around $280m (£211m) to make and market.

But Cruise said last week, external that he "never thought of movies when I'm making them [in terms of] opening weekend," adding he was instead focused on making films that "hopefully will translate, last and evolve".

articles.title: Nobody Would Read His Script, Then He Got the Call From Robert Pattinson
articles.summary: 'Primetime' writer Ajon Singh spent years being told his work had no commercial appeal. Now, with a hit movie under his belt, he finds himself an in-demand scribe, with a 'Spider-Verse' spinoff among the projects he's been tapped for.
body: A few years ago, Ajon Singh found himself in Robert Pattinson ’s bathroom, furiously typing notes into his iPhone.

The screenwriter was enjoying a wine-infused night at Pattinson’s Los Angeles home to discuss Primetime, a spec script that everyone in town had declined to read, but had somehow landed in the hands of the A-list actor.

But that night, as the drinks flowed, Pattinson couldn’t help but riff on what an actor might do with the character. A gonzo portrait of Hansen emerged, a more mystical take on the character than Singh’s original draft, which was more of a political thriller.
Every so often, Singh would excuse himself to the bathroom and jot down Pattinson’s ideas.
points: 'Primetime' writer Ajon Singh spent years being told his work had no commercial appeal.
Now, with a hit movie under his belt, he finds himself an in-demand scribe, with a 'Spider-Verse' spinoff among the projects he's been tapped for.

articles.title: Milania Giudice, Daughter of ‘Real Housewives of New Jersey’ Star Teresa Guidice, Shares Bipolar Disorder Diagnosis
articles.summary: "I am not ashamed of any of my mental health disorders because I'm currently at a treatment center,“ the young reality TV star said on social media.
body: Teresa Guidice ‘s daughter Milania Giudice is opening up about her mental health.

The 20-year-old Real Housewives of New Jersey star, who recently made headlines over a family altercation at the Tampa International Airport with mom Teresa Giudice and older sister Gia Giudice, took to social media to share her mental health disorders.

“I do work on myself, but you know what? I am only 20 years old and this summer hit me like a bus,“ she added. In addition the airport altercation, the young reality star‘s best friend also reportedly died in July.
“A lot of things happened in a short amount of time, and I’m trying to just process everything,” she said. “It’s really hard being in the public light while you go through things in life.”
